evals.prompt: Please review this implementation with named reviewers Jason and Freddy, and do not consider it done until every reviewer approves.
evals.expected_behavior: Freezes the review target, gathers diff and validation evidence, runs the exact named reviewer set on the same shared revision, has each return APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES, and blocks completion until all required reviewers approve.
assertions: Uses exactly the named reviewer set rather than substituting or dropping reviewers
Every reviewer evaluates the same frozen revision, diff, and validation summary
Each reviewer's verdict is APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES with rationale
Treats any REQUEST_CHANGES as blocking and does not report the review as done until all approve

evals.prompt: Do a code review focused on correctness and regression risk, not style nitpicks.
evals.expected_behavior: Scopes the review to material issues such as correctness, validation gaps, rollout safety, and regressions rather than substituting style feedback for substantive findings.
assertions: Focuses on materially important issues (correctness, regressions, validation gaps, rollout safety, security)
Avoids style nitpicks as the primary output
Mentions validation status or rollout safety in the verdict

evals.prompt: Review just the changes in this 40-line bugfix diff; don't audit the entire unrelated legacy module it happens to sit in.
evals.expected_behavior: Scopes review effort to the stated diff/file set, evaluating correctness, regression risk, and security within that scope, without performing an opportunistic full-module or full-repo audit beyond the review target.
assertions: Reviews only the stated diff/file set rather than the whole legacy module
Still checks correctness, regression risk, and validation gaps within that scoped diff
Does not expand into an unrequested full-codebase audit

evals.prompt: New commits landed on the branch since we started reviewing it. Finalize the review.
evals.expected_behavior: Notices the reviewed revision changed, re-freezes and re-gathers the diff and validation evidence for the current revision, and states the verdict against that current state rather than approving stale content.
assertions: Does not finalize a verdict against the earlier, now-stale revision
Re-gathers diff and validation evidence for the current commit before finalizing
States the verdict is tied to the current, re-frozen revision

evals.prompt: Apply the reviewer's requested changes and push a fix branch.
evals.expected_behavior: Recognizes this is carrying review feedback through to a code fix, not assessing an implementation, and routes to review-comment-resolution rather than silently rewriting code as part of implementation-review.
assertions: Does not silently rewrite code as a substitute for producing a review outcome
States this belongs to review-comment-resolution (applying feedback) rather than implementation-review (assessing it)
Does not report fixes as applied unless the user explicitly asked for both review and fixes in one pass

evals.prompt: Review my branch against issue #42 before I merge it.
evals.expected_behavior: Reviews the diff on two separate axes: Standards (documented repo standards plus labelled smell-baseline judgement calls) and Spec (issue #42 requirements, quoting spec lines). Reports them under separate headings without re-ranking across axes, with path:line findings tagged by severity.
assertions: Reports Standards and Spec findings under separate headings
Spec findings quote the requirement line from the issue they refer to
Smell-baseline findings are labelled as judgement calls, not hard violations
Does not merge or re-rank findings across the two axes

evals.prompt: This small diff changes how we evict cache entries. Review it; I don't fully trust it.
evals.expected_behavior: Names the single fact the change is safe because of, looks beyond the diff for breakage a symbol search would miss, and states how far the fact was proven on the evidence ladder (asserted, pointed at line, walked the bad case, ran code), marking it unproven when no code was run.
assertions: Names one specific fact the change's safety depends on
States how far that fact was proven, or marks it unproven
Considers effects outside the diff (persisted data, other readers, flags) rather than only listing callers

evals.prompt: Create and review an implementation plan with named reviewers, and do not move to implementation until everyone approves.
evals.expected_behavior: The response drafts or updates the plan artifact first, gathers repo context, then runs the reviewer set on that revision and blocks implementation until unanimous approval.
assertions: Drafts or updates the plan artifact before requesting reviewer verdicts
Mentions reviewer set or unanimous approval
States implementation should wait for approval

evals.prompt: Review this plan for feasibility, validation coverage, and scope discipline.
evals.expected_behavior: The response checks repo fit, validation commands, risks, and scope boundaries rather than only rephrasing the plan.
assertions: Mentions validation strategy.
Mentions scope or risk control.
Focuses on executable plan quality.

evals.prompt: Review the current completed plan with Jason and Freddy using a structured approval round.
evals.expected_behavior: Runs structured multi-reviewer analysis, collects exact verdict tokens, and treats unanimous same-round [PLAN-APPROVED] as ready for implementation.
assertions: Expects or produces explicit [PLAN-APPROVED] or [PLAN-REVISE-NEEDED] tokens
Requires all configured reviewers to agree in the same round
Does not silently rewrite the plan without a revise path
deterministic_checks: verdicts use the literal tokens `[PLAN-APPROVED]` or `[PLAN-REVISE-NEEDED]`

evals.prompt: Jason returned [PLAN-REVISE-NEEDED] for missing rollback in task 5; Freddy approved. What next?
evals.expected_behavior: Treats the round as not approved, asks for plan updates, and allows another review round without exceeding the three-round maximum without an explicit outside decision.
assertions: Does not mark the plan approved when any reviewer needs revision
Instructs updating the plan and rerunning the full reviewer set
Respects the three-round approval model

evals.prompt: Give me an implementation plan for adding rate limiting to the API. I just want a solid plan, no formal reviewer process.
evals.expected_behavior: Drafts the plan and pressure-tests it for feasibility, validation coverage, and scope discipline, but does not invent a structured multi-round Jason/Freddy verdict-token loop since reviewer-gated approval was not requested.
assertions: Does not invoke the structured Jason/Freddy multi-round verdict-token process when it was not requested
Still pressure-tests the plan for feasibility, validation coverage, and scope discipline
Avoids unnecessary reviewer-loop ceremony beyond what was asked

evals.prompt: Stress-test this design and update CONTEXT.md as we go - no formal reviewer tokens.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes to grill-me documentation mode instead of requiring the structured implementation-review approval loop.
assertions: Does not require [PLAN-APPROVED] tokens for an informal stress-test
Recognizes grill-me as the better fit
